rv.q: This show is like a tightly-wound top that spins frantically through slapstick, vaudeville, and camp without ever overstaying in one mode or the other.
'The Martyrdom of Peter Ohey' is still an undeniably engaging production, and one of the most stylish, inventive, anarchic farces you'll see this year.
This reviewer was frustrated that the production’s pacing didn’t allow it to develop its own weight, and the actors’ face coverings force them to shout all their lines at the same volume...
